overview: Two closely related, spore-forming Gram-positive rods within the same genus, distinguished mainly by motility, hemolysis, and the diseases they cause.
genZNote: B. anthracis stays still and means business. B. cereus swims around and just wants your leftover rice.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A non-motile, spore-forming Gram-positive rod causing anthrax, notable for its plasmid-encoded toxin and capsule.
aspects.valueB: A motile, spore-forming Gram-positive rod best known as a cause of foodborne illness (emetic and diarrheal syndromes).

aspects.label: Virulence Factors
aspects.valueA: Tripartite exotoxin (protective antigen, lethal factor, edema factor) plus an antiphagocytic poly-D-glutamic acid capsule, both plasmid-encoded.
aspects.valueB: Emetic toxin (cereulide, heat-stable) and diarrheal enterotoxins (heat-labile).

aspects.label: Clinical Presentation
aspects.valueA: Cutaneous, inhalational, or gastrointestinal anthrax; inhalational form is highly lethal.
aspects.valueB: Self-limited food poisoning — emetic type (associated with reheated rice) or diarrheal type (associated with meats/sauces).

aspects.label: Colony Morphology
aspects.valueA: Large, non-hemolytic, "Medusa head" or "ground glass" colonies with tenacious texture.
aspects.valueB: Large, spreading, beta-hemolytic colonies, often described as "frosted glass" appearance.
